scenes.visual: Title card: When Does the Tie Break?.

scenes.tts: Two inhibitions make positive feedback. But is positive feedback always enough to split two equal cells?
scenes.visual: The A and B pair from chapter three. The question appears as on-screen text.
scenes.narration: Two inhibitions make positive feedback. But is positive feedback always enough to split two equal cells?

scenes.tts: Predict. Give cell A one percent more Delta than B. Does the difference always come back larger?
scenes.caption: Predict. Give cell A 1 percent more Delta than B. Does the difference always come back larger?
scenes.visual: Prompt card: A has 1% more Delta. Does the difference grow? A small bump drawn on A.
scenes.narration: Predict. Give cell A 1 percent more Delta than B. Does the difference always come back larger?

scenes.visual: Hold on the prompt. A small timer icon.

scenes.tts: No. The difference must come back round the loop larger than it left.
scenes.visual: Text: the difference must come back larger than it left.
scenes.narration: No. The difference must come back round the loop larger than it left.

scenes.tts: Follow it round. B's Notch activity rises, and B's Delta falls. Then A's Notch activity falls, and A's Delta rises.
scenes.visual: The bump travels along four arrows: B Notch up, B Delta down, A Notch down, A Delta up.
scenes.narration: Follow it round. B's Notch activity rises, and B's Delta falls. Then A's Notch activity falls, and A's Delta rises.

scenes.tts: Each step passes the change on, multiplied by a factor. The steeper the step, the bigger the factor.
scenes.visual: Each arrow gets a small dial labelled steepness.
scenes.narration: Each step passes the change on, multiplied by a factor. The steeper the step, the bigger the factor.

scenes.tts: Multiply the factors all the way round. That product is the round-trip factor.
scenes.visual: The four dials combine into one dial labelled round-trip factor.
scenes.narration: Multiply the factors all the way round. That product is the round-trip factor.

scenes.tts: Take Collier and colleagues' nineteen ninety-six model. With steep responses, the one percent comes back as nearly six percent.
scenes.caption: Take Collier and colleagues' 1996 model. With steep responses, the 1 percent comes back as nearly 6 percent.
scenes.visual: Name card: Collier and colleagues, 1996 model, worked example with steep response curves. On screen: 1% goes out; 1.3, 2.4, 3.1, then about 5.7% comes back. Labels: round-trip factor about 5.7; small change near the even state; illustrative model.
scenes.narration: Take Collier and colleagues' 1996 model. With steep responses, the 1 percent comes back as nearly 6 percent.

scenes.tts: The difference grows, and the pair splits.
scenes.visual: The bump grows on each pass; A rises and B falls.
scenes.narration: The difference grows, and the pair splits.

scenes.tts: With shallow responses, the same one percent comes back as about a seventh of one percent.
scenes.caption: With shallow responses, the same 1 percent comes back as about 0.14 percent.
scenes.visual: On screen: 1% goes out, about 0.14% comes back. Round-trip factor below 1. The bump shrinks.
scenes.narration: With shallow responses, the same 1 percent comes back as about 0.14 percent.

scenes.tts: The difference fades. The two cells stay alike, however long you wait.
scenes.visual: A and B settle back to equal.
scenes.narration: The difference fades. The two cells stay alike, however long you wait.

scenes.tts: These numbers come from a model. They are illustrative, not measurements.
scenes.visual: Small label: illustrative model, not measured.
scenes.narration: These numbers come from a model. They are illustrative, not measurements.

scenes.tts: On a steep loop, an even pair is like a pencil balanced on its point.
scenes.visual: A pencil balanced on its point.
scenes.narration: On a steep loop, an even pair is like a pencil balanced on its point.

scenes.tts: The slightest tip grows. There are two stable outcomes: A neural, or B neural.
scenes.visual: The pencil tips left or right. Labels: A neural, B neural.
scenes.narration: The slightest tip grows. There are two stable outcomes: A neural, or B neural.

scenes.tts: A system like this is called bistable. It has two stable outcomes, and the even state between them is unstable.
scenes.visual: Label: bistable. Two valleys with a hilltop between them.
scenes.narration: A system like this is called bistable. It has two stable outcomes, and the even state between them is unstable.

scenes.tts: On a shallow loop, the pair is a marble in a bowl. Push it, and it rolls back to the middle.
scenes.visual: A marble in a bowl, rolling back to the centre.
scenes.narration: On a shallow loop, the pair is a marble in a bowl. Push it, and it rolls back to the middle.

scenes.tts: Does the size of the first difference matter much? In this example, a start ten times smaller delays the split by about a third.
scenes.visual: Two time courses, from a 1% start and a 0.1% start; the second splits a little later. Label: worked example.
scenes.narration: Does the size of the first difference matter much? In this example, a start ten times smaller delays the split by about a third.

scenes.tts: So on a steep loop, ordinary noise can start the split. Near the threshold, though, the wait grows long.
scenes.visual: Random jitter on both cells; the split happens. Beside it, a loop just past threshold, where the split takes much longer. Label: steep loop.
scenes.narration: So on a steep loop, ordinary noise can start the split. Near the threshold, though, the wait grows long.

scenes.tts: Now put the cell in a sheet. It hears the average of its six neighbours, so one neighbour's change is diluted.
scenes.visual: A hexagonal sheet. One cell, with six neighbours highlighted.
scenes.narration: Now put the cell in a sheet. It hears the average of its six neighbours, so one neighbour's change is diluted.

scenes.tts: In the model, a pair splits when the round-trip factor is above one. An ideal hexagonal sheet needs it above four.
scenes.visual: On screen: round-trip factor above 1 for a pair; above 4 for an ideal hexagonal sheet.
scenes.narration: In the model, a pair splits when the round-trip factor is above 1. An ideal hexagonal sheet needs it above 4.
scenes.caption: In the model, a pair splits when the round-trip factor is above 1. An ideal hexagonal sheet needs it above 4.

scenes.tts: When such a sheet splits from a nearly even start, about one cell in three typically wins.
scenes.visual: The sheet resolves: one dark cell in every three, spaced apart. Label: one example; edges and settings change the count.
scenes.narration: When such a sheet splits from a nearly even start, about one cell in three typically wins.

scenes.tts: That is a spaced pattern, not a guaranteed winner per cluster. Real tissues add help: a head start, a longer reach, or timing.
scenes.visual: Three labels around a cluster: head start, longer reach, timing. Label: help, not requirements.
scenes.narration: That is a spaced pattern, not a guaranteed winner per cluster. Real tissues add help: a head start, a longer reach, or timing.

scenes.tts: The notum has a head start. Its proneural levels are already uneven, so precursors arise at reproducible spots.
scenes.visual: The notum with a cluster whose proneural shading is uneven; the darkest spot becomes the SOP.
scenes.narration: The notum has a head start. Its proneural levels are already uneven, so precursors arise at reproducible spots.

scenes.tts: Try the grid in the lesson. Its feedback scale is its own, not the model's. Turn the strength up to about four or more and step time forward, and a spaced pattern appears.
scenes.visual: The lesson grid: pale at first, then a spaced pattern as the slider moves up.
scenes.narration: Try the grid in the lesson. Its feedback scale is its own, not the model's. Turn the strength up to about 4 or more and step time forward, and a spaced pattern appears.
scenes.caption: Try the grid in the lesson. Its feedback scale is its own, not the model's. Turn the strength up to about 4 or more and step time forward, and a spaced pattern appears.

scenes.tts: Between two equal cells, the tie breaks only on a steep loop. A small difference must come back larger than it left.
scenes.visual: Takeaway card: the loop must be steep. Between two cells, a small difference must come back larger than it left.
scenes.narration: Between two equal cells, the tie breaks only on a steep loop. A small difference must come back larger than it left.

scenes.visual: Hold on the takeaway card.
